instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Job 35:13 'regard' is the Almighty looking upon and taking notice of a cry: the verse says an empty cry is not heard and not regarded by him.
observations.grounds: nor does the Almighty regard it

observations.text: In Job 34:27 'regard' is giving thought and insight: those who turned aside from God gave no heed to any of his ways, with no insight into them.
observations.grounds: had no regard for any of his ways

observations.text: In 2Ch 5:11 'without regard to' is the verb of keeping or observing in the phrase about the priests' divisions: all who were present had consecrated themselves and did not hold to the order of their courses.
observations.grounds: without regard to their divisions

observations.text: In Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9 and Psa 119:117 'regard' is the verb of looking with favor and heed: the Lord had no regard for Cain and his offering, the men are to give no heed to lying words, and the psalmist asks to heed the statutes always.
observations.grounds: for Cain and his offering he had no regard

observations.text: In Ecc 12:9 'weighing' is the Preacher giving careful thought to proverbs, weighing, studying and arranging them. It is a mental act of testing and ordering, said of a wise teacher.
observations.grounds: weighing and studying and arranging many proverbs

observations.text: In Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1 'weighing' is the weight of an object in stated measures: a ring of half a shekel, bracelets of ten, and a bar of fifty, and the balances of the hair. It is a measure, with no inner operation.
observations.grounds: a gold ring weighing a half shekel

observations.text: In 1Cor 14:29 'weigh' is judging and discerning what the prophets say: the others are to assess it. The verse sets the weighing in the listeners, after two or three have spoken.
observations.grounds: let the others weigh what is said

observations.text: In Zep 1:11 'weigh out' is the traders' weighing of silver on scales; the verse says all who do so are cut off. It is the act of measuring metal, with no inner operation.
observations.grounds: all who weigh out silver are cut off

observations.text: In Ezr 8:29 'weigh' is the weighing out of the temple gifts before the priests and the heads of houses, on a scale, at Jerusalem. It is a measuring act with no inner operation.
observations.grounds: until you weigh them before the chief priests

observations.text: Considering a matter: turning attention and thought to it, looking it over, setting the heart on it. The Lord asks Satan whether he has fixed on Job, the observer sets his heart on the field and takes instruction, the Preacher looks over all his works, the generation gives no thought to the servant's being cut off, the sinner sees his transgressions and turns, the seer contemplates the horns, Joseph turns over what he resolved, and Abraham fixes his attention on his own body without his faith weakening. In each the consideration is an act of the mind taking in a matter, usually before a turn or a conclusion. Verses: Job 1:8, Job 2:3, Pro 24:32, Ecc 2:11, Isa 53:8, Eze 18:28, Dan 7:8, Mat 1:20, Rom 4:19.
observations.grounds: to pay attention, notice, observe

observations.text: Reckoning something or someone as a certain thing: how a person or thing is counted, judged or esteemed. Sarah counts the promiser faithful, Abraham concludes that God can raise the dead, Moses counts the reproach of Christ greater than treasure, rulers are held to be rulers, the silent fool is held wise, silver is counted as nothing, the men are counted reliable, the people are counted as foreigners, as sheep, as pots, the laws as strange, the potter as clay, the disciples dispute who is held greatest, the uncircumcised is counted as circumcised, servants are counted as masters worthy of honor, the Lord counts the exiles good. The word is a reckoning or valuation, the standing given by a judgment. Verses: 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20, Neh 13:13, Pro 17:28, Mar 10:42, Heb 11:11, Heb 11:19, Heb 11:26, Lev 19:23, 1Sa 1:16, Jer 24:5, 1Cor 4:1, 2Th 3:15, 1Ti 6:1, 1Pe 5:12, Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Isa 29:16, Isa 29:17, Lam 4:2, Hos 8:12, Luk 22:24, Rom 2:26, Rom 8:36.
observations.grounds: to credit, count, reckon; regard, think, consider

observations.text: Having regard: giving notice and heed to someone or something, or refusing it. The Lord has no regard for Cain's offering, the psalmist asks God to have regard for the covenant and the vine, the wicked do not regard the Lord's works, God does not regard those wise in their own conceit, Levi disregards his kin, the righteous have regard for the life of the beast, the Medes have no regard for silver, and none is shown to the priests. The word is attention that turns toward a person or matter with favor or care, or is withheld. Verses: Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9, Deu 9:27, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 25:25, 2Ki 3:14, 2Ch 5:11, 2Ch 6:19, Job 9:21, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Psa 74:20, Psa 80:14, Psa 119:117, Psa 144:3, Pro 12:10, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16.
observations.grounds: to look at or to, regard

observations.text: 'With regard to' as a linking phrase of respect: it marks the matter spoken of, a festival or a sect or the children of man or the Philistines. The words are prepositions and nouns of concern and carry no act of thinking. Verses: Judg 15:3, Ecc 3:18, Act 28:22, Col 2:16.
observations.grounds: about, concerning, in regard to

observations.text: Regarding by a standard: Paul says he knew and took account of Christ once by the standard of the flesh and now takes account of no one by it. The Greek verbs are of knowing, used for the rule by which a person is judged. Verses: 2Cor 5:16.
observations.grounds: to know, understand

observations.text: Weighing in the mind: the prophets' words are to be weighed by the others who judge them, and the Preacher weighs, studies and arranges proverbs. The word is an act of testing and judging what is said or learned. Verses: 1Cor 14:29, Ecc 12:9.
observations.grounds: weigh, test, prove, consider

observations.text: Weighing out metal on scales: the traders weigh out silver, and the gifts are to be weighed before the priests. It is the act of measuring by weight, with no act of thinking. Verses: Ezr 8:29, Zep 1:11.
observations.grounds: to weigh, weigh out, pay out

observations.text: Weight as a stated measure: a ring and bracelets of a given weight in shekels, a bar of gold of fifty shekels, and the balances of the hair. The word is the weight of an object. Verses: Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21, Eze 5:1.
observations.grounds: heaviness, weight

observations.text: The codes of considering are verbs of setting, turning and looking: H7760K and H7896K (to put, set; set mind to), H6437G (to turn), H7200H (to see, consider), H7878 (to muse), H7920 (to consider, contemplate), G2657 (to pay attention, contemplate, with intense attention) and G1760 (to reflect on). With them H3820A (heart) is the seat set on the matter, as in Job 1:8 and Pro 24:32. The lexicon bears out attention set on a matter and taken in. H0595 (I), H1934 (to be) and G3756 (not) are small words in the units of Pro 24:32, Dan 7:8 and Rom 4:19.
observations.grounds: set mind to

observations.text: The codes of reckoning are H2803H and H2803J (to think, account, esteem, reckon), G3049 (to credit, count, reckon; regard), G2233 (to think, consider, count), G1380 (to think, consider, regard), H5234A (to regard, acknowledge), H5414I (to give, set, make) and H6188 (to count uncircumcised). The lexicon bears out counting a person or thing as something, as in Heb 11:26, Isa 29:16 and 1Sa 1:16.
observations.grounds: to credit, count, reckon

observations.text: The codes of having regard are verbs of looking and heeding: H8159 (to gaze, regard), H5027 (to look, regard), H7789 (to behold, regard), H7200G (to see, regard), H0995 (to discern, give heed), H6437G (to turn toward), H6485I (to pay attention to), H8104J (to keep, give heed), H7919A (to give attention to), H3045 (to know), and H5375Q (to lift the face, show favour). The lexicon bears out regard given or withheld, as in Gen 4:5 and 2Ki 3:14. H0408 and H3808 (not) and H0853 (the object marker) are small words in the units.
observations.grounds: to look at or to, regard

observations.text: The codes of with regard to are prepositions and nouns of concern: G4012 (about, concerning, in regard to), G3313 (part, share), H1700 (cause, manner, reason) and H9006 (from). The lexicon bears out a linking phrase of respect in Judg 15:3, Ecc 3:18, Act 28:22 and Col 2:16, naming no act of thinking.
observations.grounds: about, concerning, in regard to

observations.text: The codes of regarding by a standard are G6063 and G1097, verbs of knowing (to know, recognize, understand). The lexicon gives knowing, which 2Cor 5:16 uses for the rule by which a person is regarded.
observations.grounds: to know, come to know, recognize, understand

observations.text: The codes of weighing in the mind are H0239 (weigh, test, prove, consider) and G1252 (to make a distinction, judge a dispute). The lexicon bears out testing and judging what is said or learned, in Ecc 12:9 and 1Cor 14:29.
observations.grounds: weigh, test, prove, consider

observations.text: The codes of weighing out are H8254 (to weigh, weigh out, pay out) and H5187 (laden). The lexicon bears out H8254 in Ezr 8:29; the lexicon of H5187 gives only laden, while Zep 1:11 renders it as weighing out silver: the data and the rendering differ.
observations.grounds: to weigh, weigh out, pay out

observations.text: The code of weight is H4948 (heaviness, weight). The lexicon bears out a stated weight of an object in Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1.
observations.grounds: heaviness, weight

observations.text: The surface considered carries many codes in two uses. Of attention set on a matter: H7760K with H3820A in Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 (set the heart), H7896K in Pro 24:32, H6437G in Ecc 2:11, H7878 in Isa 53:8, H7200H in Eze 18:28, H7920 in Dan 7:8, G1760 in Mat 1:20, G2657 in Rom 4:19. Of counting as something: H2803H in 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20 and Neh 13:13, H2803J in Pro 17:28, G1380 in Mar 10:42, G2233 in Heb 11:11 and Heb 11:26, G3049 in Heb 11:19. H0595, H1934 and G3756 are small words in the units.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: The surface regard carries over twenty codes in three uses. Of looking and heeding: H8159 in Gen 4:5, Exo 5:9 and Psa 119:117, H5027, H7200G, H6437G, H7789, H0995 in Psa 28:5, H7919A, H6485I, H3045, H8104J, and H5375Q in 2Ki 3:14 (to lift the face). Of counting as something: H2803H, H5234A, H5414I, H6188 in Lev 19:23, G3049, G2233, and G6063 with G1097 in 2Cor 5:16. Of a link of respect: H9006 in Judg 15:3, H1700 in Ecc 3:18, G4012 in Act 28:22, G3313 in Col 2:16. H0408, H3808, H0853 and H3820A are small words in the units.
observations.grounds: they do not regard the works of the Lord

observations.text: The surface regarded carries four codes, all of counting as something: H2803H in Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2 and Hos 8:12, H2803J in Isa 29:16 and Isa 29:17, G1380 in Luk 22:24, G3049 in Rom 2:26 and Rom 8:36.
observations.grounds: Shall the potter be regarded as the clay

observations.text: The surface weigh carries three codes: H8254 in Ezr 8:29, weighing the gifts on scales, H5187 in Zep 1:11, whose lexicon gives laden though the verse renders it weighing out silver, and G1252 in 1Cor 14:29, judging what the prophets say. Two are weighing by measure, one is weighing in the mind.
observations.grounds: let the others weigh what is said

observations.text: The surface weighing carries two codes: H4948 in Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1, the weight of an object in shekels or the balances, and H0239 in Ecc 12:9, the Preacher's weighing of proverbs in the mind.
observations.grounds: weighing and studying and arranging many proverbs

observations.text: A negator reaches the regard itself in Gen 4:5, Deu 33:9, 1Sa 1:16, 1Sa 25:25, Job 9:21, Job 34:27, Job 35:13, Job 37:24, Psa 28:5, Isa 5:12, Isa 13:17, Isa 33:8, Lam 4:16, 2Th 3:15 and 2Cor 5:16: the regard is withheld (no regard, regard not, do not regard, regard no more, regard no one). The other qualifiers of these verses reach other words: very (the anger), cruel and wise of other persons.
observations.grounds: he had no regard

observations.text: In Gen 31:15, Isa 29:17 and Rom 2:26 the negator opens a question that expects yes: are we not regarded as foreigners, will not the field be regarded as a forest, will not the uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision.
observations.grounds: Are we not regarded by him as foreigners

observations.text: Where the word is counting as something, the qualifier gives the value counted: forbidden in Lev 19:23, wise in Pro 17:28, good in Jer 24:5, earthen against precious in Lam 4:2, strange in Hos 8:12, greatest in Luk 22:24, rulers in Mar 10:42, worthy of all honor in 1Ti 6:1, faithful in Heb 11:11 and 1Pe 5:12, able in Heb 11:19, greater in Heb 11:26; in 1Ki 10:21 silver is counted as nothing, and in Isa 29:16 the negators reach the maker's work, not the counting.
observations.grounds: considered him faithful who had promised

observations.text: Where the word is attention set on a matter, the qualifiers describe what is considered or the one considering, not the act: Job is blameless and upright in Job 1:8 and Job 2:3, the body is as good as dead in Rom 4:19, the horns are another, little and three in Dan 7:8, the land is of the living in Isa 53:8, the Preacher is wise in Ecc 12:9, the prophets two or three in 1Cor 14:29; in Mat 1:20 and Eze 18:28 the negators reach fear and death.
observations.grounds: a blameless and upright man

observations.text: Where regard is given, the qualifiers name who gives it or what stands against it: in Pro 12:10 righteous names the one whose regard reaches even his animal, set against the cruel mercy of the wicked; in 2Ki 3:14 the oath on the Lord who lives frames Elisha's regard for the king.
observations.grounds: Whoever is righteous has regard for the life of his beast

observations.text: Where the word is a weight or a link, the qualifiers reach the objects or the matter: two bracelets in Gen 24:22, a beautiful cloak, 200 shekels and a bar of 50 in Jos 7:21, a sharp sword in Eze 5:1; in Col 2:16 the negator reaches the passing of judgment and with regard to is a link; in Act 28:22 everywhere reaches the speaking against the sect.
observations.grounds: a bar of gold weighing 50 shekels

observations.text: God is named as the one who gives or withholds regard: the Lord to Cain in Gen 4:5, the Almighty to the empty cry in Job 35:13, God to the wise in their own conceit in Job 37:24, the Lord to man in Psa 144:3, the Lord to the exiles in Jer 24:5, and the Lord who will regard his people no more in Lam 4:16.
observations.grounds: nor does the Almighty regard it

observations.text: God is named as the one asked to regard or not to regard: not the stubbornness of the people for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in Deu 9:27, the prayer of his servant in 2Ch 6:19, the vine in Psa 80:14.
observations.grounds: have regard to the prayer of your servant

observations.text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 the Lord names Job as the one to be considered and puts the question to the one he speaks to: the considering is asked of another, and Job, God's servant, is its object.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: In Psa 28:5 and Isa 5:12 the Lord is named as the one whose works and deeds people do not regard.
observations.grounds: they do not regard the deeds of the Lord
